newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end down after record high.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end down after record high.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended down on Wednesday after the composite index hit a record high earlier, with the impact of the economic deregulation package announced on Monday waning, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index ended down 2.70 points, or 0.36 percent, at 738.14 after touching a record 742.95 points earlier.
Decliners led advancers by 86 to 52 with 59 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at 574 billion rupiah.
"Players took profit on a lack of fresh market factors as the impact of the deregulation package appeared to wane," one analyst with a foreign brokerage firm said.
Brokers and analysts said the market was likely to consolidate in the coming days, with profit-taking seen mostly in the banking and property sectors.
"The goverment's move to limit bank loans to the property sector is likely to weaken sentiment on the property sector in the near term," another analyst said.
Indonesia's central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said on Wednesday a curb on property loans was needed because a policy of moral suasion had not been effective enough.
He said property loans as a percentage of total credits rose to 19.61 percent in April 1997 from 12.2 percent in December 1992, with commercial banks posting the highest growth.
Most property stocks were among the losers due to the weak sentiment on the sector, brokers said.
Brokers, however, said local players continued to actively buy second-liners due mostly to speculative reasons.

Tyre manufacturer Gajah Tunggal was among the most active stocks on news reports that it planned to supply tyres to automotive firm PT Timor Putra Nasional, producer of Indonesia's so-called national car, brokers said.
Gajah Tunggal ended unchanged at 1,375 rupiah, with some 17 million shares traded, after touching a day high of 1,500 rupiah.
